name: cdn-grey-budget
description: Two of the four published edge prefixes are 'grey': a TCP flow to an address in them may send six packets (SYN and ACKs included) and is then silently cut. A TLS handshake gets about that far; a tunnel never does. The other two prefixes are clean. Op cdn: the route carries, on an edge in a clean prefix — the edge picker's failure-state probe (more than ten packets) must move on from the grey ones.
analogue: net4people #676 (18 Oct 2026, one author): TCP to some Cloudflare addresses cut a few packets after the handshake; the reason the plan's edge picker (B-6) probes with a >10-packet exchange instead of a handshake. Model: a fixed count of client packets per flow, per /26, silent drop. Not modelled: a budget in bytes or time, one that differs per hour or per ISP, or one counted on both directions (the box sees the client's packets only).
